newsitem.title: UK: UK still needs rapeseed imports after record crop.
newsitem.headline: UK still needs rapeseed imports after record crop.

text.p: Britain's rapeseed output should total a record 1.35 million tonnes in 1996 but imports of 200,000 tonnes will still be required to meet domestic needs, leading food group Dalgety plc said on Thursday.
"This year's oilseed rape harvest is probably the best on record," Paul Rylott, national seed product development manager at Dalgety Agriculture told a news conference.

Rylott said the estimated 1996 output figure was some 250,000 tonnes higher than last year from a similar crop area. But Britain will still need to import rapeseed despite its increased output, he said.

"Although U.K. production is 1.35 million tonnes, exports are likely to reach 100,000 tonnes which will still leave the U.K. requiring some 200,000 tonnes of imports to meet domestic requirements," he said.

Overall winter rape yields were 4.00 tonnes per hectare and spring yields averaged around 2.5 tonnes per hectare, although many crops all over the country had yielded well in excess of 5.0 tonnes per hectare, he said.
"With yields down in other parts of the world and consequently prices remaining firm, the future of the crop continues to be healthy," Rylott said.
"...with new developments in designer oils now only just around the corner, the crop's profitability should increase still further," he added.
Dalgety Agriculture is the agribusiness arm of Dalgety plc. --Jeremy Smith, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8064
